title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is section 1 of a note on the 'extended special Teichmüller group of the cylinder' X = U×I, with U the unit circle and I = [-1,1]. The goal is to model the mapping class group of the annulus, relative to its boundary and including orientation reversal, by an explicit Lie-group action on the universal cover. The boundary-fixing part should come out as Z (the Dehn twist).

Step 1, formula (8). The real dihedral group D_R = {1,σ}⋉R, with σuσ^{-1} = -u, acts on each covering line R_ε (the cover of the boundary circle U_ε) by (σ^ν.u).t = (-1)^ν(t+u): translate by u, then possibly reflect. This is a genuine left action. For example (σ.u)(σ.v) = (v-u) in D_R, and both sides send t to t+v-u.

Step 2, formula (9). The action normalises the deck group Z, so it descends. It gives an action of D_R on U_ε, and, after dividing by the kernel Z of D_R → D_U ≅ O(2), an action of D_U = {1,σ}⋉U on U_ε by z ↦ (zθ)^{±1}. This is the standard action of O(2) on the circle (rotation, then complex conjugation).

Step 3, the boundary. D_R×D_R acts factorwise on ∂X~ = R_{-1} ⊔ R_1, lifting the action of D_U×D_U on ∂X = U_{-1} ⊔ U_1.

Step 4, the interior. The action is to be extended to X~ = R×I, which covers X by (t,s) ↦ (e^{2πit}, s), formulas (10)–(11). For this Grothendieck restricts to the subgroup D_{R×R} = {1,σ}⋉(R×R), formula (12). Here σ acts diagonally, so both boundary circles are reflected simultaneously; this is required for the reflection to extend to the cylinder.

Step 5, completed on the next page. (u_{-1}, u_1) acts by (t,s) ↦ (t+u_s, s), where u_s is the affine interpolation of the two values, and σ acts by (t,s) ↦ (-t, s). The kernel on ∂X is Z×Z. Its image in Homeo(X) is:
- for n_1 ≠ n_{-1}, the twist z ↦ z·e^{2πi(n_1-n_{-1})(s+1)/2}, i.e. a power of the Dehn twist;
- for the diagonal (n,n), the identity.
So this models the mapping class group of the annulus rel boundary, π_0 = Z, inside a 'rigidified' extended group. It is a building block for Grothendieck's Teichmüller 'Lego' (surfaces with boundary, gluing along circles, with orientation reversal included).
errors: No mathematical errors found on this page. The formulas (8), (9) and (12) are consistent group actions.
Minor notational looseness: (8) writes the action on R_ε with labelled points t_ε, while (9) uses dotted points ż_ε for the induced action on U_ε.
The claim that D_R itself acts on U_ε is true (it acts through D_U), but this is left implicit.
The restriction to the diagonal-σ subgroup in (12) is motivated only implicitly: an independent reflection of a single boundary circle does not extend to the cylinder.

ideas.what: Universal covering group of O(2) realised as the real dihedral group {1,σ}⋉R, acting on the universal cover of the circle, with exact sequence 1→Z→D_R→D_U→1.
ideas.modern_name: Universal cover of O(2) / lift of the O(2) action on S^1 to R

ideas.what: Action of {1,σ}⋉(R×R) on the cylinder via affine interpolation between the two boundary translations. The boundary-trivial kernel Z×Z maps onto the Dehn twists, and the diagonal acts trivially.
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of the annulus rel boundary ≅ Z (Dehn twist); extended mapping class group of the annulus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn; classical (cf. Farb–Margalit, A Primer on Mapping Class Groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and the role of the cylinder and its twists in gluing, but not this explicit model

ideas.what: Using rigidified (universal-cover) symmetry groups of boundary circles to define 'special extended' Teichmüller groups of bordered surfaces, as a basis for gluing (Lego).
ideas.modern_name: Framed/parametrised boundary mapping class groups; extended mapping class groups in the Teichmüller tower / modular functor framework

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard setup: the universal cover of O(2) acting on the cylinder, with the Dehn twist emerging as the boundary-trivial kernel. It is of mild archival interest as Grothendieck's explicit conventions for boundary-parametrised extended Teichmüller groups. Nothing here is mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: Line after (8): read 'en une opération de D_R sur U_ε et en une de D_U sur U_ε'; the struck-out symbol before U_ε is a crossed-out letter.
The line '∂X~ = U~_{-1} ⊔ U~_1 ≃ R~_{-1} ⊔ R~_1' is better read as ≃ R_{-1} ⊔ R_1 (the covering lines of (3)).
In (12) the subscript is D_{R×R} and the image of σ^ν.(u_{-1},u_1) is (σ^ν.u_{-1}, σ^ν.u_{+1}); the '1/2 direct' annotation (semidirect) sits under {1,σ}.
'qui va faire opérer' should likely read 'que l'on va faire opérer'.
